messages:
Anya: quick check — onboarding user hitting 401 when streaming from a Windows GH Actions runner, using an env file we committed to the runner secrets. Anyone seen CRLF/newline padding bite the basic auth header before?
Mike: yup, seen that. often it's a trailing \r or extra space in the secret that makes `Authorization: Basic` mismatch. :grimacing:
Lisa: can you paste the header you're constructing (sanitized) and how the secret is loaded?
Anya: we do `AUTH_HEADER=$(echo -n \"$API_KEY\" | base64)` in a step, then `curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $AUTH_HEADER\" https://api.redwood.example/stream` — key is from GH secret `API_KEY` set on repo. runner is windows-latest.
Pranav: windows runner often has CRLF when someone edits the secret on Windows Notepad. Also GH secrets copy/paste can include invisible BOM. Quick test: `printf %s "$API_KEY" | od -An -t x1` to see trailing 0d/0a or ef bb bf.
Anya: nice. i tried `echo "$API_KEY" | base64` earlier which might append newline. suggestion for robust one-liner?
Mike: use `echo -n` or better `printf %s "$API_KEY" | base64` — `echo -n` isn't always consistent on PowerShell. On windows agent, run a bash step (runs on MINGW/msys) or use `pwsh -c "$env:API_KEY.Trim()`
Lisa: also verify header format: for Basic auth it's base64 of `username:password`. if you're just sending APIKEY as the whole basic value, ensure server expects that. Our SDKs accept `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and also `Authorization: Basic <base64>` for legacy clients, so mismatch happens often.
Anya: ahh — they had code that expected `Authorization: Basic base64(api_key:)` (note trailing colon). i didn't realize. so the header was wrong.
Pranav: yep. sample: `printf %s \"$API_KEY:\" | base64` — that appends the colon. we recommend `Bearer` for new integrators to avoid this confusion.
Anya: for streaming specifically, do we have any proxy that rewrites headers or strips `Authorization`? Customer uses corporate proxy.
Mike: corp proxies sometimes drop `Authorization` for websockets or streaming. if using `nginx` as a forward proxy it might remove `Authorization` for `Upgrade: websocket` unless configured. Also some TLS terminating proxies re-inject a different header.
Lisa: to isolate: try `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Basic $AUTH_HEADER\" -N \"https://api.redwood.example/stream\"` from the runner to see debug. `-v` will show what got sent client-side; if 401 still, capture tcpdump or ask ci-bot to upload logs.
ci-bot: uploaded logs to https://ci-artifacts.redwood.local/1854321999/stream-debug.log :robot_face:
Anya: posted contents: server complains "invalid credentials" and curl shows header set correctly client-side. so proxy likely mutating it.
Pranav: next step: bypass proxy if possible (use a test VM in same network without proxy) or set `--proxy ''` to disable curl proxy env. Also inspect `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION` vs `Authorization` — some proxies change case.
Mike: small PS note: when building basic header in Go, use `base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(apiKey+":"))` not string concatenation with `\n` etc. i keep seeing folks accidentally include `\n`.
Lisa: i'll add a short blurb to devex FAQ: 1) prefer `Authorization: Bearer` 2) if using Basic, ensure correct `username:password` base64 format (empty password -> trailing colon) 3) trim CR/LF/BOM from secrets 4) use `printf` / trim helpers in CI 5) check proxy rewriting.
Anya: thanks — saved the team a bunch of hair-pulling. will update the onboarding doc and ping infra to check proxy rules.
Mike: if you want, i can add a small GH Actions snippet to the docs that normalizes secrets and prints hex debug (non-printing) on a safe var.
Anya: would love that. cheers :pray:
Pranav: fwiw, also seen streaming clients fail if they set `Expect: 100-continue` header inadvertently; should be fine but worth checking.
Lisa: noted, closing loop when infra confirms proxy. :white_check_mark:
